title: Ireland – Education and training services – Communications, online learning enhancement, and scientific advisory - UCC-VEAT-2024-06
description: This is a voluntary ex-ante transparency (VEAT) notice. This notice acknowledges that University College Cork (UCC) contracted with Evenflow SRL, for the provision of communications support, scientific advisory and technical expertise for online learning enhancement, for the Copernicus Atmospheric Monitoring Service and Copernicus Climate Change Service, under the competitively won ECMWF Service Contract CJS2_156b_UCC. Under CJS2_156b_UCC, UCC is leading a Service team to provide support to the ECMWF in implementing training events and online learning resources for the two Copernicus Services. Evenflow SRL will lead the communications activities for the overall Service contract, provide technical support to promote online and in-person training, enhance the online training offering, and contribute to the Scientific Advisory Committee. Evenflow SRL were uniquely placed in terms of skillsets, professional networks and relationships to perform this role in the overall Service contract. They specialise in the promotion, exploitation and market uptake of innovative technologies (primarily in the areas of Earth Observation and Satellite Navigation). Their role is centred on promotion and communications management of all information pertaining to training events and online learning content releases implemented by the Service, for which they are uniquely suited. Evenflow are already embedded in the ECMWF’s Copernicus community, providing communications support to the ECMWF in terms of their more general Copernicus communications. As such, they were uniquely placed to complement this Service, ensuring it can quickly and effectively align with the standards and procedures of Copernicus communications by the ECMWF. Evenflow are also technically and thematically equipped to play a key front-end role in enhancing the online Training offering of both the Copernicus Services, complementing the skills of the wider Service team with their niche user-facing expertise. In addition, with their track record in strategic advisory, and supporting the promotion, exploitation and market uptake of technologies noted above, they have the required expertise in satellite data uses, applications and business development to contribute their market perspectives to the Service’s Scientific Advisory Committee - a key Quality Control mechanism embedded within the contract Service – in addition to bringing their highly beneficial professional networks into the Service. This is in close alignment with the requirements of the overarching Service contract between UCC and the ECMWF, specifically to deliver high-quality, customised training and developing learning resources for Copernicus services that are quality controlled to a standard of high scientific rigour. The company was therefore selected to participate in the bid for the CJS2_156b ITT as their unique combination of skillsets, technical expertise, capabilities and networks complemented those of the bidding consortium, completing it’s offering to the ECMWF. They were integral to the awarded bid, and have been contracted accordingly.

title: GHG emission reduction potential of EU-related maritime transport and its impacts.
description: The contract should lead to the identification of the marginal abatement costs in the sector and the no-regret GHG emission reduction potential from maritime transport up until 2030. No-regret means that the costs associated with the emission reduction, such as investment costs, operational costs or carbon costs, remain lower than the savings, especially fuel savings, generated by the emission reduction.In particular, the contract should define the in-sector cost-effective GHG emission reduction, as well as the overall cost-effective contribution from maritime transport to tackle climate change, including through the purchase of offsets/allowances from other sectors.The contract should also carry out a sensitivity analysis underlying the relevant parameters leading to a variation of GHG emissions from maritime transport. In particular, impacts of changes in GDP and its geographical distribution, fuel price variations and improvement of design and operational energy efficiency should be clearly pointed out.

title: Germany – Pharmaceutical products – Abschluss einer nicht-exklusiven Rabattvereinbarung nach § 130a Abs. 8 SGB V zum Wirkstoff Formoterol (ausschl. Dafo. DOS), ATC R03AC13 für die Zeit 01.07.26 - 30.06.28 (zzgl. V.-Option 1x12 Monate)
description: § 130a Absatz 8 SGB V ermöglicht den Krankenkassen und pharmazeutischen Unternehmen, Rahmenrabattverträge über die zu Lasten der gesetzlichen Krankenkassen abzugebenden Arzneimittel zuschließen. In Hinblick auf die dafür einschlägigen gesetzlichen Vorschriften zur Vergabe öffentlicher Aufträge, findet ein regelmäßiger Prozess wirkstoffbezogener, förmlicher Vergabeverfahren nach den Regularien des 4. Teils des GWB durch die DAK-Gesundheit statt. Für vom Bieter näher in der Anlage 2 zum Vertrag zu benennende Arzneimittel zu dem o. g. Wirkstoff Formoterol (ausschließlich Darreichungsform DOS), ATC R03AC13, beabsichtigt die DAK-Gesundheit, bis zum Inkrafttreten neuer Arzneimittelrabattverträge mit möglichst allen interessierten pharmazeutischen Unternehmen Arzneimittelrabattverträge abzuschließen. Ein Rabattvertrag i.R.d. Zulassungsmodells zu dem o. g. Wirkstoff tritt erstmals am 01.07.2026 in Kraft und endet am 30.06.2028 (zzgl. Verlängerungsoption 1x12 Monate). Er endet unabhängig davon automatisch mit Inkrafttreten des Exklusivvertrages.
